slides_detail.title: Demography
slides_detail.text_content: Demography Bolangir's demographic profile reflects a district undergoing a steady demographic transition while retaining its predominantly rural character. Population growth has moderated alongside declining fertility, and improvements in life expectancy point to gradual gains in health and survival. The district is entering a favourable phase with a growing working-age population, offering an opportunity to accelerate economic growth and improve livelihoods before population ageing becomes more pronounced. Despite a relatively balanced sex ratio and modest urbanization, much of Balangir's population continues to reside in rural areas, where access to quality education, healthcare, and employment remains uneven. Together, these trends position the district at a critical juncture, where investments in human capital, rural development, and inclusive economic opportunities will determine how effectively it can translate its demographic dividend into long-term development. slides_detail.title: Health & Nutrition
slides_detail.text_content: Health & Nutrition Bolangir has made steady progress in improving maternal and child health, with reductions in child mortality and improvements in several nutrition indicators reflecting better access to essential health and nutrition services. However, the district continues to face significant challenges. Healthcare infrastructure remains limited relative to the needs of its largely rural population, while high levels of anaemia among children and women continue to pose a major public health concern. Although chronic undernutrition has declined, persistent micronutrient deficiencies and gaps in healthcare access underscore the need for sustained investments in preventive healthcare, nutrition interventions, and strengthening primary healthcare systems to improve overall health outcomes.

slides_detail.title: Education
slides_detail.text_content: Education Bolangir has made notable progress in expanding access to education, with high enrolment at the elementary level and strong transition rates between preparatory, middle and secondary stages. However, learning continuity remains a challenge, as dropout rates increase significantly at the secondary level, particularly among vulnerable groups. The district's education system is predominantly government-run, supported by favourable pupil-teacher ratios that provide a conducive learning environment. At the same time, gaps in digital infrastructure persist, with only a limited proportion of schools equipped with functional smart classrooms, highlighting the need for greater investment in technology-enabled learning and improved educational infrastructure to enhance learning outcomes and retention.

slides_detail.title: Geography
slides_detail.text_content: Geography Bolangir's geography is closely tied to its agrarian economy, with agriculture serving as the primary livelihood for much of the population. The district's landscape comprises extensive cultivable land interspersed with forested areas, while seasonal rainfall largely determines agricultural productivity. Although irrigation infrastructure has expanded over the years, farming continues to rely significantly on monsoon conditions, making crop production vulnerable to rainfall variability. The predominance of lift irrigation schemes reflects efforts to improve water access and reduce dependence on rain-fed agriculture. Strengthening irrigation efficiency, sustainable water management, and climate-resilient farming practices will be critical to enhancing agricultural productivity, improving rural livelihoods, and building resilience against climatic uncertainties.

slides_detail.title: Demography
slides_detail.text_content: Demography Kalahandi's demographic story is one of rapid transformation. Once characterised by sustained population growth and relatively high fertility, the district is now moving swiftly through the demographic transition as family sizes shrink and population growth slows. This shift is gradually reshaping its age structure, with a growing working-age population offering a window of opportunity for economic development even as the share of older persons continues to rise. Although tribal communities remain an important part of the district's social fabric, Kalahandi's demographic profile is more diverse than many neighbouring districts. Improvements in the sex ratio and life expectancy reflect steady gains in health and well-being, while the district's predominantly rural character and limited urbanization continue to influence access to services and livelihoods. As Kalahandi transitions towards a more mature population structure, its long-term development will depend on effectively harnessing its demographic dividend while preparing for the challenges of an ageing population. slides_detail.title: Health & Nutrition
slides_detail.text_content: Health & Nutrition Kalahandi's health and nutrition landscape reflects a district where progress in healthcare delivery has begun to translate into better outcomes, but significant gaps remain. Expanded health infrastructure and improved access to services have contributed to reductions in child mortality and a steady decline in multiple forms of child undernutrition, signalling gradual improvements in maternal and child health. Despite these gains, neonatal survival continues to be a major concern, pointing to the need for stronger antenatal, delivery, and newborn care. Anaemia also remains deeply entrenched among women and children, limiting overall health gains and highlighting persistent nutritional deficiencies. Going forward, improving the quality of maternal and newborn care, strengthening nutrition programmes, and expanding preventive healthcare will be essential to sustaining progress and reducing avoidable health disparities across the district.

slides_detail.title: Education
slides_detail.text_content: Education Kalahandi's education sector reflects steady progress in expanding access and improving student retention, making it one of the stronger-performing districts in the region. High enrolment at the elementary level and strong transition rates into secondary education indicate that most children are able to remain in the school system through the foundational years. Government schools continue to anchor educational provision, complemented by a growing presence of private institutions, while favourable pupil–teacher ratios and expanding digital infrastructure have strengthened the learning environment. However, a substantial gender gap in literacy persists, highlighting continuing disparities in educational attainment between men and women. Bridging this gap, while further improving the quality of teaching and expanding access to technology-enabled learning, will be key to ensuring more equitable and inclusive educational outcomes.

slides_detail.text_content: Geography Kalahandi's geography is defined by a diverse landscape of fertile plains, forested hills, and river valleys that have long shaped its economy and settlement patterns. Extensive forest cover coexists with productive agricultural land, while major rivers provide vital water resources that sustain farming across the district. The hilly tracts are rich in mineral resources, giving Kalahandi significant potential for mining and industrial development alongside agriculture. However, the varied terrain also presents challenges for connectivity and service delivery in remote areas. Balancing agricultural growth, responsible mineral extraction, environmental conservation, and improved infrastructure will be central to the district's sustainable and inclusive development.

Kalahandi.demography_narrative: Kalahandi's demographic story is one of rapid transformation. Once characterised by sustained population growth and relatively high fertility, the district is now moving swiftly through the demographic transition as family sizes shrink and population growth slows. This shift is gradually reshaping its age structure, with a growing working-age population offering a window of opportunity for economic development even as the share of older persons continues to rise. Although tribal communities remain an important part of the district's social fabric, Kalahandi's demographic profile is more diverse than many neighbouring districts. Improvements in the sex ratio and life expectancy reflect steady gains in health and well-being, while the district's predominantly rural character and limited urbanization continue to influence access to services and livelihoods. As Kalahandi transitions towards a more mature population structure, its long-term development will depend on effectively harnessing its demographic dividend while preparing for the challenges of an ageing population.

Kalahandi.health_narrative: Kalahandi's health and nutrition landscape reflects a district where progress in healthcare delivery has begun to translate into better outcomes, but significant gaps remain. Expanded health infrastructure and improved access to services have contributed to reductions in child mortality and a steady decline in multiple forms of child undernutrition, signalling gradual improvements in maternal and child health. Despite these gains, neonatal survival continues to be a major concern, pointing to the need for stronger antenatal, delivery, and newborn care. Anaemia also remains deeply entrenched among women and children, limiting overall health gains and highlighting persistent nutritional deficiencies. Going forward, improving the quality of maternal and newborn care, strengthening nutrition programmes, and expanding preventive healthcare will be essential to sustaining progress and reducing avoidable health disparities across the district.

A relatively balanced sex ratio and improving life expectancy reflect steady gains in health and survival outcomes, while the gradual rise in the elderly population signals the onset of population ageing. Together, these trends place Kendujhar at an important demographic juncture, offering the potential to harness its demographic dividend while preparing for the long-term challenges of an ageing population. slides_detail.title: Health & Nutrition
slides_detail.text_content: Health & Nutrition Kendujhar's health and nutrition profile reflects both encouraging progress and persistent public health challenges. Maternal and child mortality have declined over time, indicating improvements in healthcare delivery, while a relatively low maternal mortality ratio points to better maternal care. The district's network of primary health centres, community health centres, and sub-centres has expanded access to basic healthcare, although limited hospital bed availability continues to place pressure on health services. Nutrition outcomes present a mixed picture: chronic child undernutrition has improved, but acute malnutrition, underweight prevalence, and anaemia among children and women remain widespread, highlighting persistent deficiencies in dietary diversity and micronutrient intake. These challenges suggest that while healthcare access has steadily improved, strengthening nutrition interventions, preventive healthcare, and health infrastructure remains essential for achieving better health outcomes across the district.

slides_detail.title: Education
slides_detail.text_content: Education Kendujhar's education sector has made significant progress in expanding access to schooling, supported by a strong network of government schools that continue to serve the vast majority of students. Enrolment at the primary level remains high and transition rates between school stages are encouraging, reflecting improved retention through the elementary years. However, dropout rates rise noticeably at the secondary level, indicating challenges in sustaining participation beyond compulsory education. Despite favourable pupil–teacher ratios and growing access to digital infrastructure such as computer facilities and smart classrooms, a substantial gender gap in literacy persists, with women continuing to lag behind men. Overall, Kendujhar's education system has established a solid foundation in access and infrastructure, but improving gender equity, reducing secondary school dropout, and enhancing the quality of learning remain key priorities.

slides_detail.title: Geography
slides_detail.text_content: Geography Mayurbhanj's geography is defined by its forests, hills, and fertile plains, making it one of Odisha's most ecologically diverse districts. Situated on the fringes of the Chotanagpur Plateau and home to the Similipal landscape, its terrain has long shaped patterns of settlement, livelihoods, and development. Extensive forest cover coexists with a predominantly agrarian economy, where cultivation continues to depend heavily on the monsoon despite gradual improvements in irrigation. While agricultural infrastructure has expanded over time, the district's rugged terrain and forested landscape continue to influence land use, accessibility, and economic activity, reinforcing Mayurbhanj's identity as a predominantly rural, forest-dependent district.

slides_detail.text_content: Geography Koraput's unique geography has shaped its identity, economy, and development trajectory. Nestled in the Eastern Ghats, the district is characterised by rugged hills, dense forests, river valleys, and a cooler climate that distinguishes it from much of Odisha. Its rich natural landscape, marked by prominent peaks, waterfalls, and perennial rivers, supports exceptional biodiversity while sustaining agriculture and tribal livelihoods. At the same time, the hilly terrain and dispersed settlements have historically posed challenges for connectivity and service delivery. Today, Koraput's scenic beauty and ecological wealth offer significant opportunities for sustainable tourism, conservation, and nature-based livelihoods, making it one of Odisha's most distinctive and resource-rich districts.

slides_detail.text_content: Health & Nutrition Malkangiri's health and nutrition landscape reflects incremental progress amid enduring structural challenges. Improvements in healthcare access and the expansion of primary health facilities have contributed to gradual reductions in maternal and child mortality, extending essential services to the district's remote tribal communities. Nutrition outcomes have also shown encouraging signs, with declines in child undernutrition indicating steady gains in food and nutrition security. However, the district continues to face serious public health concerns. Maternal health outcomes remain among the weakest in the state, while widespread anaemia among women and children points to persistent micronutrient deficiencies and gaps in preventive care. Sustained investments in primary healthcare, maternal and child health services, nutrition interventions, and last-mile service delivery will be essential to improving overall health outcomes in this geographically challenging district.

Malkangiri.demography_narrative: Malkangiri is undergoing a gradual demographic transition while retaining its predominantly tribal and rural character. Population growth has moderated over time as fertility begins to decline, although the district continues to have a relatively young population and a growing working-age cohort that offers significant development potential. Home to a large tribal population, including two Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), Malkangiri's social and cultural identity remains deeply rooted in its indigenous communities. Improvements in life expectancy and a steadily strengthening sex ratio reflect positive demographic trends, but limited urbanization and geographic isolation continue to influence access to services and economic opportunities. As the district moves through this phase of demographic change, strengthening human capital, connectivity, and livelihood opportunities will be essential to ensuring that its demographic potential translates into inclusive and sustainable development.

Malkangiri.health_narrative: Malkangiri's health and nutrition landscape reflects incremental progress amid enduring structural challenges. Improvements in healthcare access and the expansion of primary health facilities have contributed to gradual reductions in maternal and child mortality, extending essential services to the district's remote tribal communities. Nutrition outcomes have also shown encouraging signs, with declines in child undernutrition indicating steady gains in food and nutrition security. However, the district continues to face serious public health concerns. Maternal health outcomes remain among the weakest in the state, while widespread anaemia among women and children points to persistent micronutrient deficiencies and gaps in preventive care. Sustained investments in primary healthcare, maternal and child health services, nutrition interventions, and last-mile service delivery will be essential to improving overall health outcomes in this geographically challenging district.

slides_detail.title: Demography
slides_detail.text_content: Demography Mayurbhanj's demographic story is deeply intertwined with its tribal heritage and forested landscape. As one of Odisha's most rural and tribal-majority districts, it has witnessed steady population growth for more than a century, although the pace of growth has gradually moderated in recent decades. Today, the district is entering a favourable demographic phase, with its working-age population at an all-time high, presenting a valuable opportunity to accelerate economic growth and improve livelihoods. A relatively balanced overall sex ratio further strengthens this demographic advantage. Yet, important challenges remain. Literacy levels continue to trail the state average, with women facing particularly significant educational disadvantages. At the same time, the child sex ratio points to persistent gender bias at birth, tempering the otherwise positive picture of gender balance. Mayurbhanj therefore stands at a pivotal demographic juncture—well positioned to harness its demographic dividend, provided that development is inclusive and reaches its diverse tribal and rural communities. slides_detail.title: Health & Nutrition
slides_detail.text_content: Health & Nutrition Mayurbhanj's health and nutrition story is one of progress constrained by persistent structural challenges. While most families readily seek medical care, the health system remains overstretched, with shortages of doctors, specialists, and diagnostic facilities often forcing patients to travel outside the district for advanced treatment. High poverty levels further limit healthcare choices, making government facilities the primary source of care. Nutrition outcomes present an equally mixed picture: despite improvements in chronic child undernutrition and expanding maternal healthcare services, acute malnutrition and anaemia remain widespread, pointing to persistent gaps in dietary quality and micronutrient intake rather than healthcare access alone. Child mortality continues to be shaped by preventable birth-related complications, while malaria remains a recurring public health challenge in the district's tribal and forested areas. Together, these realities highlight a health system that is steadily improving but continues to face significant constraints in delivering equitable health and nutrition outcomes.

slides_detail.title: Education
slides_detail.text_content: Education Mayurbhanj's education landscape reflects steady progress alongside persistent inequalities. While access to schooling is widespread and enrolment at the elementary level remains strong, sustaining students through secondary education continues to be a challenge as dropout rates increase with age. The district's education system is anchored largely by government schools, supported by favourable pupil–teacher ratios that indicate adequate classroom staffing. However, learning outcomes are constrained by uneven infrastructure, with limited access to modern digital teaching facilities despite growing availability of basic computer resources. Most importantly, a pronounced gender gap in literacy continues to define the district's educational profile, highlighting the need for greater investment in girls' education and retention. Overall, Mayurbhanj has made significant strides in expanding educational access, but improving equity, retention, and the quality of learning remains central to building a more inclusive education system.

slides_detail.title: Geography
slides_detail.text_content: Geography Mayurbhanj's geography is defined by its forests, hills, and fertile plains, making it one of Odisha's most ecologically diverse districts. Situated on the fringes of the Chotanagpur Plateau and home to the Similipal landscape, its terrain has long shaped patterns of settlement, livelihoods, and development. Extensive forest cover coexists with a predominantly agrarian economy, where cultivation continues to depend heavily on the monsoon despite gradual improvements in irrigation. While agricultural infrastructure has expanded over time, the district's rugged terrain and forested landscape continue to influence land use, accessibility, and economic activity, reinforcing Mayurbhanj's identity as a predominantly rural, forest-dependent district.

Strengthening primary healthcare, maternal and child nutrition, and preventive health services will be critical to sustaining recent progress and improving long-term health outcomes.

slides_detail.title: Education

Strengthening girls' education, improving retention beyond the elementary stage, enhancing teacher availability at higher grades, and expanding digital learning infrastructure will be essential to achieving more equitable and better-quality educational outcomes in the district.

slides_detail.title: Geography
slides_detail.text_content: Geography Nabarangpur's geography is defined by its forested plateaus, fertile river valleys, and predominantly rural landscape, which have shaped both livelihoods and settlement patterns. Situated in the southwestern part of Odisha, the district is characterised by extensive forest cover, gently undulating terrain, and the Indravati River system that supports agriculture and water resources. The region receives abundant monsoon rainfall, sustaining a predominantly agrarian economy while reinforcing its dependence on rain-fed cultivation. Rich deposits of minerals add to the district's natural resource base, offering opportunities for economic development alongside agriculture. At the same time, dispersed tribal settlements, forested terrain, and limited connectivity continue to pose challenges for infrastructure development and service delivery, underscoring the need to balance economic growth with environmental conservation and inclusive rural development.

slides_detail.title: Demography
slides_detail.text_content: Demography Rayagada's demographic profile reflects a district in the midst of a gradual demographic transition. Population growth has slowed steadily as fertility declines, although family sizes remain relatively larger than in many other parts of Odisha. The district's strong tribal identity, including the presence of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), continues to shape its social and cultural landscape. A favourable sex ratio and improving life expectancy point to positive demographic and health outcomes, while the expanding working-age population presents an opportunity to accelerate inclusive economic growth before population ageing becomes more pronounced. Despite modest urbanization, Rayagada remains overwhelmingly rural, with dispersed tribal settlements influencing access to services and livelihoods. Together, these trends position the district at a critical stage where investments in health, education, livelihoods, and tribal development will be key to translating its demographic potential into sustainable and equitable development. slides_detail.text_content: Health & Nutrition Rayagada's health and nutrition profile reflects encouraging improvements in healthcare alongside persistent public health challenges. Declining maternal and child mortality indicate gradual gains in healthcare access and service delivery, supported by an expanding network of primary health facilities that has improved outreach across the district's remote and hilly regions. Nutrition outcomes present a mixed picture: while acute and chronic undernutrition have shown signs of improvement, malnutrition continues to affect a large share of children, and anaemia has emerged as a critical public health concern among both women and children. These trends underscore the need to complement improvements in healthcare delivery with stronger nutrition programmes, maternal and child health interventions, and sustained efforts to address the underlying socio-economic determinants of poor health.

slides_detail.title: Geography
slides_detail.text_content: Geography Rayagada's geography is defined by the rugged hills, forests, and river valleys of the Eastern Ghats, which have profoundly shaped its settlement patterns, livelihoods, and development. The district's undulating terrain, dense forest cover, and network of rivers support rich biodiversity while sustaining agriculture and the livelihoods of its predominantly tribal population. Fertile river valleys provide the main areas for cultivation, whereas the surrounding hills and forests continue to influence connectivity and access to services. This distinctive landscape has preserved Rayagada's ecological wealth and cultural heritage, but it has also contributed to geographic isolation, making infrastructure development and service delivery more challenging. Balancing environmental conservation with improved connectivity and sustainable livelihoods remains central to the district's long-term development.

Strengthening girls' education, improving retention beyond the elementary stage, enhancing teacher availability at higher grades, and expanding digital learning infrastructure will be essential to achieving more equitable and better-quality educational outcomes in the district.

slides_detail.title: Geography
slides_detail.text_content: Geography Nabarangpur's geography is defined by its forested plateaus, fertile river valleys, and predominantly rural landscape, which have shaped both livelihoods and settlement patterns. Situated in the southwestern part of Odisha, the district is characterised by extensive forest cover, gently undulating terrain, and the Indravati River system that supports agriculture and water resources. The region receives abundant monsoon rainfall, sustaining a predominantly agrarian economy while reinforcing its dependence on rain-fed cultivation. Rich deposits of minerals add to the district's natural resource base, offering opportunities for economic development alongside agriculture. At the same time, dispersed tribal settlements, forested terrain, and limited connectivity continue to pose challenges for infrastructure development and service delivery, underscoring the need to balance economic growth with environmental conservation and inclusive rural development.

These challenges suggest that while healthcare access has steadily improved, strengthening nutrition interventions, preventive healthcare, and health infrastructure remains essential for achieving better health outcomes across the district.

slides_detail.title: Geography
slides_detail.text_content: Geography Mayurbhanj's geography is defined by its forests, hills, and fertile plains, making it one of Odisha's most ecologically diverse districts. Situated on the fringes of the Chotanagpur Plateau and home to the Similipal landscape, its terrain has long shaped patterns of settlement, livelihoods, and development. Extensive forest cover coexists with a predominantly agrarian economy, where cultivation continues to depend heavily on the monsoon despite gradual improvements in irrigation. While agricultural infrastructure has expanded over time, the district's rugged terrain and forested landscape continue to influence land use, accessibility, and economic activity, reinforcing Mayurbhanj's identity as a predominantly rural, forest-dependent district.

slides_detail.text_content: Education Nabarangpur's education sector has made steady progress in expanding access to schooling, with strong enrolment at the elementary level and government schools serving as the backbone of the education system. However, significant challenges remain in ensuring that children, particularly girls, complete their education. A wide gender gap in literacy continues to reflect persistent educational inequalities, while dropout rates increase sharply at the secondary level, limiting progression to higher education. Although digital infrastructure and access to computer facilities have improved, technology-enabled learning remains uneven, with relatively few schools equipped with smart classrooms. Strengthening girls' education, improving retention beyond the elementary stage, enhancing teacher availability at higher grades, and expanding digital learning infrastructure will be essential to achieving more equitable and better-quality educational outcomes in the district.

slides_detail.title: Geography
slides_detail.text_content: Geography Nabarangpur's geography is defined by its forested plateaus, fertile river valleys, and predominantly rural landscape, which have shaped both livelihoods and settlement patterns. Situated in the southwestern part of Odisha, the district is characterised by extensive forest cover, gently undulating terrain, and the Indravati River system that supports agriculture and water resources. The region receives abundant monsoon rainfall, sustaining a predominantly agrarian economy while reinforcing its dependence on rain-fed cultivation. Rich deposits of minerals add to the district's natural resource base, offering opportunities for economic development alongside agriculture. At the same time, dispersed tribal settlements, forested terrain, and limited connectivity continue to pose challenges for infrastructure development and service delivery, underscoring the need to balance economic growth with environmental conservation and inclusive rural development.
